findings.description: The new prose still leans on bare prohibitions: "never paste a file tree, a pseudocode block or a whole function" (L77), "Never paste a log" (L81), "never restate the diff or the commit list" (L52). writing-for-agents/SKILL.md:74 asks you to state the target behaviour instead ("Trim output to the one line that matters"), or to pair a guardrail with a positive target.

The example defines the `removed` and `changed` classDefs but only uses `added`. The feature, fix, perf and refactor templates tell the agent to mark nodes with these classes but don't carry the `classDef` lines. An agent copying only a template gets unstyled nodes. Say once that L72-74 is the palette to paste, or point the templates at it.

The new template table gives every row a conventional type except "a revert" and "a task from a `pup` session". The agent doesn't know which title type to use for those two kinds. Add `revert` to the Title format type list, or say which type each one takes.

Body rules (SKILL.md:170) say to end every body with `Lands decision NN.` / `Follow-up to #NNNN.`. Only the feature, fix, adr and session templates carry that line, while chore, perf, refactor, revert and test do not. Say that those templates add the anchor only when it applies, or add the line to them.

refactor.md:19 and revert.md:15 hardcode `**Door:** two-way`. SKILL.md:85-87 makes a destructive or `SCHEMA`/`MIGRATIONS` change one-way, and a refactor or revert that touches the store can be one. Use the `<one-way or two-way>` placeholder the other templates use.
perf.md's Evidence is a measurement table plus a method line. SKILL.md:81 says Evidence is "One line each for before and after". Note the perf exception in SKILL.md so the two files don't disagree.

The Title format still shows `<type>(<scope>): <summary> (PROJ-XXXX)`, and the length lint counts `(PROJ-XXXX)`, yet L147 and L45 say this repo has no tracker id. Drop the id from the format and from the lint.

Other skills still cite the removed `docs/09-decisions.md`, among them writing-for-agents:87, domain-modeling (SKILL.md, DECISION-FORMAT.md), tdd, wayfinder, to-spec, to-tickets, diagnosing-bugs, wait-what, codebase-design/DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md and skills/README.md. They now disagree with pr-description, which this PR moved to `docs/adr/`.

process_issues.description: The briefs gave the PR-copy path as `.claude-pr/skills/...`, but the real path is `.claude-pr/.claude/skills/...`. The conventions reviewer couldn't find the PR files, so it worked from `gh pr diff 233` and the base copies, and its line numbers were approximate. The orchestrator re-anchored them against the PR copies.
